new.asserts:
Let $Y$ be a finite nonempty response set with a fixed enumeration $(y_1,\ldots,y_m)$, and let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on $Y$ satisfying $p(y)>0\Rightarrow q(y)>0$. Define $\rho(y)=p(y)/q(y)$ when $q(y)>0$ and $\rho(y)=0$ when $q(y)=0$. Then, for every real-valued function $f$ on $Y$,

$$\sum_{j=1}^{m}q(y_j)\rho(y_j)f(y_j)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}p(y_j)f(y_j).$$

In particular, $\sum_{j=1}^{m}q(y_j)\rho(y_j)=1$. This is a finite response identity; it asserts no change-of-measure result on an arbitrary trajectory space.

new.asserts:
Fix a prompt $q$, an open parameter set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, and the finite response policy with nonempty fixed support $(b_1,\ldots,b_m)$ and score vectors $S_\theta(q,b_j)$ from the generation protocol. For any fixed finite reward function $r$ on that support, define

$$J(\theta):=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\pi_\theta(b_j\mid q)r(b_j).$$

Then, for every $\theta\in U$,

$$\mathbb E_\theta[S_\theta(q,Y)\mid q]=0,\qquad \mathbb E_\theta[r(Y)S_\theta(q,Y)\mid q]=\nabla_\theta J(\theta).$$

new.asserts:
Fix a prompt $q$, a parameter $\theta$ in the open domain of its finite response policy, a finite real reward function $r$ on the policy support, and an integer $G\ge2$. Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_G$ be independent responses with common law $\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid q)$, let $R_i:=r(Y_i)$, let $S_i:=\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(Y_i\mid q)$, and set
$\overline R:=G^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{G}R_j$ and $J(\theta):=\mathbb E_\theta[r(Y)\mid q]$.
Then
$$\mathbb E_\theta\left[\frac1G\sum_{i=1}^{G}(R_i-\overline R)S_i\mid q\right]=\left(1-\frac1G\right)\nabla_\theta J(\theta).$$
If instead $\overline R_{-i}:=(G-1)^{-1}\sum_{j\ne i}R_j$, then
$$\mathbb E_\theta\left[\frac1G\sum_{i=1}^{G}(R_i-\overline R_{-i})S_i\mid q\right]=\nabla_\theta J(\theta).$$

new.asserts: Let a prompt have one correct response $c$ with probability $3/4$ and one incorrect response $w$ with probability $1/4$. With a perfect verifier $A=C$, rejection search with budget $N=2$ returns an accepted response with probability $15/16$. With a false-positive verifier that accepts both $c$ and $w$, rejection search always returns its first draw, so its false-acceptance probability is $1/4$; the per-draw union bound gives $2(1/4)=1/2$.

new.asserts: For one prompt let the finite response law assign mass $1/4$ to a correct response $c$ and mass $3/8$ to each of two incorrect responses $w_1,w_2$. Let the verifier accept $c$ and $w_1$ but reject $w_2$. The single-response pass@1 rate is $1/4$; for any integer $M\ge1$, the empirical pass@1 over $M$ independent replicas from this same law has expectation $1/4$. Oracle pass@2, the event that at least one of two independent candidates is correct, has probability $7/16$; verifier-selected accuracy, the probability the rejection-search output is correct conditional on its being accepted, is $2/5$.
